title: Predicting Crime by Time: Hours, Days, Paydays & Festive Spikes
simple_summary: Crime does not happen at random times. Burglaries happen when homes are empty (work hours or summer holidays). Street robberies spike on payday weekends and late Friday nights. Forecast.ETS in Excel projects future counts from historical weekly rhythms without coding.
key_concept: Moving Averages & 95% Confidence Intervals: Projections are never guaranteed certainties. They show an expected range (dashed line + shaded band) so commanders know the uncertainty.
recommended_action: Align patrol shift changeovers so officers are on the street during the 20:00 - 23:30 surge rather than handing over vehicles at the station.

dataset_sample.factor: Month-end salary payout + weekend bars closing
Festival shopping rush, crowded jewelry markets
Late-night residential entry when occupants sleep
City-wide celebrations, alcohol disorder, street clashes

non_tech_takeaway: Predictions beyond 4-6 weeks out get shaky. Always refresh your time forecasts monthly and brief your team with the shaded confidence band, not a single hard number.
